newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, gilt prices steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, gilt prices steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended at 1.50-2.00 percent on Thursday, down from the day's opening level of 2.50-3.25 percent, dealers said.
"Call rate will continue to stay at low levels, market is still waiting and watching the sentiments," a dealer at an insurance company said.
There were more sellers in the securities market than buyers, but investors were hesitant to put money in the securities, a dealer at state-run bank said.
"Wait and watch the 91 day treasury bill auction on Friday, it can change the sentiments," he said.
"Call rate has been touching bottoms, but yields on securities are not moving in tandem with call rates," a dealer at Centurion Bank said.
Trade on the National Stock Exchange fell to 1.93 billion rupees against Wednesday's 2.79 billion rupees, dealers said.

The market saw trades in 4 to 5 year maturity papers, while the latest auctioned five year maturity paper saw some trades in the range of 100.05 rupees to 100.09 rupees against the issue price of 100 rupees and Reserve Bank's offer price of 100.10 rupees, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India auctioned five year paper on November 26 for 20 billion rupees.
The zero coupon bond maturing in 2000 rose by 10 basis points to 62.30 rupees, while 13.50 percent 1997 stock was unchanged at 102.60 rupees, dealers said.
The yield on treasury bills maturing in January 1997 fell to 8.20 percent on Thursday, compared to the previous close of 8.54 percent

Commercial papers were quoted 12.0-14.0 percent for 91 days for P1+ rated companies and 13.5-15.0 percent for P1 rated companies. Certificates of deposit were at 12-13.50 percent for P1+ rated companies, dealers said.
